Hi Liza — thanks for the clear asks. High level answers up front: 

- Invoice cadence: Redwood issues an annual committed-spend invoice (covering the committed amount) at activation, followed by monthly drawdown statements that reduce the prepay balance. For customers that prefer, we can switch to quarterly invoicing with monthly drawdowns; defaults are annual invoice + monthly ledger entries.
- Meter format: Yes — we can provide a CSV with the exact columns you listed. We also include a ledger_key that maps to your ERP account.

I attached a proposed timetable and the CSV header spec for your AP team to validate. Notes in the sheet: 
- Invoice release rail: activation invoice on day 0, monthly reduction statements on the 1st of each month (UTC), and a reconciliation run on the 15th of the following month.
- VAT routing: see the companion VAT_Routing_Table (Kim will confirm entity remit rows below).
- PO/ERP: we can include an invoice_number prefix (BRG-2028-ANNUAL) if you need it for matching.

Next steps: 
1) Kim to confirm EU VAT vs UK VAT handling and whether Brightline will provide a VAT-exempt certificate for any entity.
2) If that looks good, I’ll finalize the RI_Invoice_Timetable_2028.xlsx and share a DocuSign bundle for the invoice schedule + SOW terms.

Subject: VAT routing notes and remit entity mapping (Brightline)

Hi Liza — looping in the VAT routing details you requested. Quick notes: 

- Entity remit matrix: Redwood has three possible remit entities for Brightline payments (US, Redwood EU B.V., Redwood UK Ltd). The choice depends on the customer billing country and whether Brightline provides a valid VAT registration.
- If Brightline will self-account for VAT (reverse charge) in the EU, provide the VAT ID per EU entity and we’ll tag invoices accordingly. If not, Redwood EU B.V. will collect VAT on the invoice.
- UK: we can issue from Redwood UK Ltd and include a VAT line if required.

I attached a CSV (VAT_Routing_Table.csv) that maps typical country -> remit_entity -> tax_treatment. Please review the rows highlighted in yellow (UK and Germany) — those require confirmation. Also flagged a special-case: if you remit from Brightline Ireland entity, we need the EORI/VAT confirmation for cross-border reconciliation.

A couple operational clarifications: 
- Reconciliation cadence: monthly statement on the 1st, adjustments on the 15th. We post ledger entries to your ERP-friendly CSV with a 'ledger_key' column.
- Credit application: prepay balance is applied FIFO against monthly consumption entries unless you request a specific allocation.

If you confirm the remit entity for UK and Germany by EOD Tuesday (2028-04-02), Marissa and I will finalize the routing rows and Jonas will issue the DocuSign for signature.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
